title: A Learjet carrying nine people crashed in a Palm Beach County neighborhood
dek: The FAA says the jet left Austin for the Bahamas and went down near homes. Video spread within the hour, and so did guesses about the cause that no agency has backed.
what: The Federal Aviation Administration says a Learjet 60 crashed at about 12:50 p.m. Eastern on Sunday 1 November in a residential area near Cresthaven, Palm Beach County, Florida. WFLX, citing the FAA, reports that the jet had left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, with nine people aboard. Palm Beach County Fire Rescue said Military Trail was closed between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North. Video from the scene shows flames, thick black smoke and debris across the road.

The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating, and the NTSB leads. The FAA called its details preliminary and subject to change. The NTSB says it is sending a go-team. No cause has been established.

CBS Miami reports that all nine people aboard were killed and that no one on the ground was reported hurt. It says Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the nine deaths, and that about 600 people were evacuated from a nearby mobile home park. CBS Miami also reports air traffic control audio in which the pilot says the jet is in an overspeed condition and descending fast, then declares an emergency. Posts from Breaking911 and Fox News say there were no survivors. Fox News also says the jet came down miles from Mar-a-Lago. I did not check the Fox details.

Some posts tie the crash to Mar-a-Lago, which is in Palm Beach. Secular Talk host Kyle Kulinski asks in a post whether the administration shot down a business jet. The post gives no evidence. I found no statement from the FAA, the NTSB or the military about any such thing, and the FAA names no cause.
why: The video is short, close and dramatic, the jet fell near homes, and the site is near a place that is often the subject of airspace rumours. Accounts that collect breaking news posted it first, and claims about the cause followed.
next: The NTSB preliminary report, and the names of the dead once officials release them.
